source.description: Public fictional Davies workbook; read-only source capture. This is not a blank household template.

coverage.read: Every grid in the 21-tab public fictional workbook at its reported bounds.
coverage.retained: All user-entered values outside raw input rows; all formulas, data-validation rules, notes and number formats. Identical rules and formats are grouped into contiguous row ranges.
coverage.omitted: Fictional raw values in Transactions A2:J, Payslips A2:G and Valuations A2:C. Visual styles other than number formats, merges, chart objects, permissions and bound scripts are not captured.
coverage.limits: Source material for an adapted template, not a validated new-household template or complete visual clone.

yes lets the bound Apps Script serve every tab as JSON to anyone with its URL (fine for a fictional sheet, never for real money). Anything else and the feed answers with a refusal.
Demonstration workbook. Every person, account, institution and amount here is fictional. Data runs from 1 July 2025 to the As-of date in Settings, one month closed at a time.
Settings, Accounts, Categories, Loans, Assets, Subscriptions, Goals
Set up once, changed by a person. Blue text marks the cells you can change.
One row per real-world event, append only. Imports or an AI agent add rows here and nowhere else. Correct a mistake with a new row, not by editing history.
Cash Flow, Budget, Savings Finder, Mortgage Scenarios, Tax Forecast, Compliance Checks, Net Worth
Formulas only. Each tab answers one question. Never type into them.
The contract for anything that draws pictures: one row per headline number with a fixed Metric ID, value, unit, period and comparison.
Bank, payslip and valuation records land in the raw data tabs.
Helper columns on those tabs add the month, financial year, category, group and tax treatment by looking up the input tabs.
Each view summarises the raw data for one question.
Metrics pulls the headline numbers from the views.
Charts, emails, Claude artifacts or a phone widget read Metrics and the views. They never need to know how a number was worked out.
Money in is positive and money out is negative in the raw data. Views show spending as positive numbers.
Moves between the household's own accounts (including card payments) have Flow = Transfer and are left out of income and spending.
The As-of date in Settings drives every view. Change it and the months, financial year and comparisons roll forward.
July to June, labelled by the year it ends: FY26 is 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026.
Accounts start ACC-, loans LN-, transactions T0001 onwards. Views look rows up by ID, so IDs never change once used.
Blue text: inputs. Black text: formulas. Green text: links to another tab.
What the sample data is built to show
Three streaming services nobody has used for months, a free trial that became a paid plan, and two cloud storage plans doing the same job.
Netflix, Spotify and Kayo prices went up, health insurance rose in April and car insurance rose 18% at renewal.
A foreign transaction fee on every ChatGPT charge, and interest plus a late fee after the card was not paid in full at Christmas.
Two identical same-day charges, at JB Hi-Fi and Uber Eats.
Dining and takeaway climbs month by month through 2026.

A $1,849 laptop claimed in full with no receipt, a $12,800 kitchen recorded as a repair, and a crowdfunding payment recorded as a donation. Tax Forecast shows the refund as claimed and again once those claims are fixed, so the amount at risk is visible.
Rate-rise stress test, the effect of the offset account, extra repayments and a refinance comparison.
Three uncategorised transactions. Salary deposits, payslips and transfers all reconcile, so those checks pass.
An agent appends rows to Transactions, Payslips or Valuations using IDs that exist in the input tabs. It does not edit views or Metrics.
For a summary, read Metrics first, then the view behind any number that needs explaining.
Compliance Checks is the first place to look after an import. Unknown categories, duplicates and one-sided transfers show up there.

Append the month's bank rows, payslips and one valuation per item in Assets dated the month end. Update Last used in Subscriptions and work-from-home hours in Settings. Then move the As-of date. The month is closed when every Close check in Compliance Checks is OK; until then Metrics close.items_missing is above zero and dashboards should say so.
Estimates using published resident rates and simple rules. Not tax advice. Check current rates at ato.gov.au.
The current-year tax forecast scales the year to date to a full year. One-off deductions are not scaled.
Property, super and share values are fictional month-end figures, not market data.
One row per metric. Charts, emails and dashboards read this tab by Metric ID, so the IDs never change.

Money in and out by month, in dollars. Transfers between the household's own accounts are excluded. Spending shows as positive numbers.

Current financial year to date, by category, in dollars. Monthly bills are paced by months elapsed. Lumpy bills (quarterly or annual) are measured against their full-year budget, so a renewal does not read as overspending.
Each row is a formula over the raw data. Recurring savings are per year. One-off items are money to recover.

Tax and data-quality checks over the raw data. Review means look at the rows before relying on the tax forecast.
A claim can be denied without written evidence.
Work equipment over the immediate-deduction limit
Items over the limit are depreciated over their effective life, and only the work-use share counts.
Renovating or replacing a whole asset is usually a capital improvement, not a deductible repair.
Only gifts to registered charities, with a receipt, are deductible. Crowdfunding for a person usually is not.
Rental property ran at a loss (prior year)
A rental loss is allowed, but keep every record that supports it.
A gap means a missing pay or a deposit in the wrong category.
They are left out of budgets and tax totals until categorised.
A typo in a category ID drops the row from every view.
Same merchant, amount, account and day. Usually a double charge worth disputing.
Transfers that do not net to zero
A one-sided transfer means an account feed is missing.
Interest means the card was not paid in full that month.
Rows dated after the as-of date are left out of every view.
Valuations missing for the as-of date
Property, super, shares, the car and both loans read as zero until their month-end values are entered, so net worth and the mortgage are wrong.
Valuations, one row per item in Assets
Salary deposits without a payslip (current year)
Gross pay and tax withheld come from payslips, so the tax forecast is wrong until every pay has one.
Bank import missing for the latest month
An everyday account or card with no rows this month usually means its statement was not imported.
Subscriptions charged but not on the list
A new subscription, often a free trial that rolled into a paid plan, is invisible to the usage and price checks until it is on the list.
Usually the same statement imported twice. Views look rows up by ID, so every ID must be used once.
